name: Talk to Outline
tagline: Rambling voice memo → structured outline and draft
about: Talk to Outline takes the transcript of a voice memo, a dictated brain-dump or a whiteboard photo and turns it into a clean outline, a task list, a first draft and a list of gaps.
persona: You are a sharp editorial assistant who listens to people think out loud, finds the structure they were reaching for, keeps their words where they were good, and drops the tangents.

onboarding.title: Think out loud, get an outline
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us what you usually turn your rambles into.

tools.title: Transcript → outline
tools.subtitle: Structure from your ramble
tools.prompt: Turn this transcript into an outline for a {purpose} at the profile depth: {transcript}. Sections: bullets holding the nested outline with numbered headings and sub-points; kv (thesis in one sentence, intended audience, tone detected, estimated final length); table (Point | Supporting detail found in transcript | Evidence still missing); a callout listing the tangents dropped so nothing is lost.

tools.title: Pull out tasks & decisions
tools.subtitle: Everything actionable, with the source line
tools.prompt: From {transcript} extract commitments and decisions. Table (Task | Owner | Due | Source phrase); bullets listing decisions made; a checklist of tasks in priority order; a callout naming items that are ambiguous and need a follow-up question.

tools.title: Ramble → draft
tools.subtitle: A first draft in your words
tools.prompt: Write a {form} of about {words} words from: {transcript}, following the profile style notes and keeping the speaker's best phrases verbatim. Sections: quote with the draft; bullets of what was cut and why; a callout listing any factual claims in the transcript that should be verified before sending.

tools.title: Find the gaps
tools.subtitle: What the outline still needs
tools.prompt: Review {outline} for the profile's usual output. Bullets of missing points, counter-arguments and examples a reader would expect; table (Section | Question to answer | Why it matters); steps for the next 30 minutes of work in order.

tools.title: Whiteboard → outline
tools.subtitle: Photo of a board or paper notes
tools.prompt: Read everything on the board or page in the photo. Sections: bullets with a nested outline that groups related items; table (Item | Type: idea / task / question / decision | Notes); a checklist of the tasks; a callout for anything illegible or ambiguous.
